verdict.rationale: TeamViewer's own marketing describes a built-in AI agent, Tia, that 'rapidly fix[es] IT issues', a natural-language AI troubleshooting assistant, and an AI note-taker that compiles case summaries, so a built-in assistant clearly exists. The evidence mostly shows answering questions and summarizing, not users handing off tasks for it to carry out, and it comes only from marketing-page snippets. missing for 10: documented task delegation and execution workflow (what actions the assistant can take, approvals, scope), in-depth first-party docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Tia, your AI agent, learns from every support session to predict, prevent, and rapidly fix IT issues.
By querying our AI troubleshooting assistant, find faults and fix them fast, using natural language to get real-time, device-specific answers and insights.
Session Insights: Our AI-powered note-taker compiles a summary for each case, spots patterns, highlights insights
